design.summary: A curated, touch-responsive procedural-art studio that converts parameterized GPU scenes into saveable compositions.
design.brainstorm_concept: An interactive art application where users create evolving visual compositions using procedural shaders, particles, noise fields, fluid effects, mathematical patterns, and geometric forms.
design.primary_capability: visual parameter editor, deterministic GLSL art, export/presets
design.validity_risk: reproducible image, project schema and export fidelity
capabilities: Shader pipelines and shader asset management
design.opportunity: A polished creative tool with beautiful built-in scenes, customization, saved compositions, and potentially export or sharing features.
audiences: Casual makers wanting attractive output without code
Visual artists exploring iterative procedural imagery
journeys: Open gallery, preview a scene, enter live edit, adjust palette and motion, save a named composition.
Reopen a saved composition and verify the same seed and parameter values restore the scene.
Export one full-resolution still after checking the crop and resolution.
mvp_features: Four genuinely distinct scene families: gradient noise, raymarched shapes, geometric tiling and particles
Parameter panel with constrained ranges, immediate previews and reset
Seed-based reproducibility and gallery presets
Versioned local document store with favorites and duplication
Still export via offscreen render with proper color space and aspect handling
Scene pause, scrub time and accessibility-friendly motion reduction
non_goals: Social accounts, cloud sharing and subscription infrastructure
Timeline editing and multi-pass user-authored graphs
later_ideas: Shareable preset format with integrity checks
Video export and user shader authoring

domain_types.name: ShaderParameter
domain_types.contract: ShaderParameter(id, units, minimum, maximum, default, UITransform)

algorithm_decisions: Separate document determinism from wall-clock animation; render using stored seed plus explicit simulation time.
Validate parameter schemas before uploading uniforms; define migration rules when effects change.
Prefer analytic shader scene families before adding heavy simulation; compose in linear light then present in sRGB.
Keep previews cancellable and thumbnails cached by scene version, seed and parameter hash.
render_stages: Load preset and validated parameter values.
Build per-scene uniforms and allocate shader resources through VisualCore.
Execute scene program, optional simple effect pass and tone/color mapping.
Present to ANGLE/EGL-backed surface; offline still export reuses the same render path with a separate target.
design.engineering_rule: First independent art consumer should test VisualCore shader registry, parameter uniforms, presets and export without linking ProjectM engine code.
fixtures: Given same seed and explicit time, parameter serialization round-trips and image comparison remains within defined GPU tolerances
Corrupt or future schema versions surface a recoverable error
Rapid palette edits do not leak programs, textures or FBOs
Export dimensions and alpha/color profiles match user selection
Background/foreground recreation restores scene without stale GL handles
profiling: Measure 30/60 fps configurations on target devices, avoid hard guarantees before benchmarks.
Keep compilation off the interaction critical path where supported; cache verified binaries only when valid.
Reduce iteration counts and resolution before dropping interaction frames.
risks: Preset migrations can silently change visual results—version presets and retain snapshot fixtures
Shaders may compile differently across devices—track compile logs and maintain low-complexity fallbacks
Export at large sizes can exceed GPU limits—tile or cap according to queried limits

design.summary: A tactile ink-and-fluid playground driven by a bounded GPU-feedback simulation with clear quality presets.
design.brainstorm_concept: A touch-driven simulation for colorful ink, smoke, liquid, pigment, and flowing visual effects.
design.validity_risk: timestep stability, mass/energy and resize recovery
design.opportunity: A visually satisfying creative toy with simple interactions and high-quality results.
audiences: Families and casual players who want immediate visual response
Creators seeking satisfying ink, smoke and dye compositions
journeys: Swipe to inject pigment and velocity; pinch to change brush radius.
Switch dye palette and simulation viscosity; reset to a known starting state.
Pause, step a frame, resume and capture a still.
mvp_features: 2D velocity and dye fields on a bounded simulation grid
Multi-touch splat input with capped injection rate and smooth resampling
Adjustable viscosity, dissipation and pressure iteration quality
Distinct ink, smoke and glowing-dye palettes
Pause, reset, deterministic seeded test mode, and still capture
Configurable simulation resolution with thermal downgrade
non_goals: Unbounded particle emission or background compute
later_ideas: Advanced vorticity confinement and multi-layer media

domain_types.name: FluidConfiguration
domain_types.contract: FluidConfiguration(gridWidth, gridHeight, timeStep, pressureIterations, dyeDissipation, velocityDissipation, viscosity)

algorithm_decisions: Use semi-Lagrangian advection for MVP, with explicitly documented numerical diffusion.
Compute divergence, iterative pressure estimate and velocity projection using ping-pong framebuffers.
Clamp delta time and cap splat count to avoid instability after a long app suspension.
Define coordinate and framebuffer orientation; no read/write feedback to the same bound texture.
Expose test-mode fixed time step and seed; document that the model is artistic, not physical validation.
render_stages: Drain and normalize touch splats.
Apply velocity and dye injection pass.
Advect velocity and dye; compute divergence; run pressure Jacobi passes; subtract pressure gradient.
Composite dye with display palette and bloom; present via existing ANGLE-backed render host.
design.engineering_rule: The fluid solver must be an isolated app-domain component with a reference CPU test implementation for a handful of tiny grids, not a new VisualCore renderer.
fixtures: Uniform dye at rest decays only according to configured dissipation
Zero-velocity test keeps a known dye pattern bounded
Boundary modes have fixture tests and no out-of-bounds sampling
Every ping-pong pass writes to a different target from its sampled input
Suspend/resume causes bounded catch-up, not hundreds of solver steps
profiling: Baseline low resolution first; expose quality tiers with measured frame time.
Track per-pass timing if supported, memory footprint and dye field resolution.
Gracefully reduce pressure iterations before reducing touch responsiveness.
risks: FBO formats and texture filtering support vary—probe actual ANGLE/GL ES capabilities and select fallback formats
Solver cost grows with screen size and iterations—separate simulation from presentation resolution
High-frequency touch events may overwhelm input—coalesce and bound queues

domain_types.contract: FractalView(centerX, centerY, scale, aspect, mode, juliaCReal, juliaCImag)

algorithm_decisions: Pixel-to-complex mapping must account for aspect ratio and resolution-independent gesture updates.
Implement escape-time iteration and smoothed color bands with explicit guard against NaN/Inf.
Audit float precision on target ANGLE-backed devices before promising deep zoom; employ documented emulated double or CPU tile fallback only if needed.
Calculate preview with reduced iteration count while user is moving, then refine at rest.
render_stages: Map touch/camera state into complex plane.
Dispatch shader for escape-time count and smooth escape value.
Apply independently controlled color palette and optional supersampling.
Composite guidance overlay and present; use offscreen high-resolution path for capture.
design.engineering_rule: Render precision must be presented as an engineering limitation of the selected ANGLE/OpenGL ES shader path, not solved by silently introducing a Metal renderer.
fixtures: Known points: Mandelbrot origin interior, c=2 outside, and known Julia samples
Zoom under centered pinch keeps selected complex coordinate stationary
Aspect-ratio changes preserve center and avoid distortion
Precision-warning thresholds are based on measured/known representation limits
Saved bookmarks round-trip and reproduce views within tolerances
profiling: Profile panning frame pacing independently from high-quality settled render.
Bound GPU loops and adapt iteration count to zoom and interaction.
Test landscape, portrait and split-view display transforms.
risks: 32-bit precision causes jitter or blank screens at deep zoom—do not market unbounded zoom
Extreme iteration counts can freeze UI—cap and add asynchronous refinement
Gesture transform bugs accumulate—use double on CPU view state and stable coordinate transforms

algorithm_decisions: Begin with a deterministic fixed-step CPU reference for small populations and compare GPU behavior later.
Use bounded acceleration, damping, respawn rules and border wrap/reflect semantics.
Pick buffer/texture-backed state update based on audited GL ES features; avoid unsupported compute assumptions.
Use decay ping-pong render targets for trails and separate simulation from presentation resolution.

Update particles with fixed timestep and capped substeps.

Decouple visual sparkle from high physical particle count.
Set quality policy from measurements on at least one low- and one high-end device.

domain_types.contract: GeometryPreset(kind, symmetryOrder, repeats, paletteID, seed, camera, schemaVersion)

algorithm_decisions: Implement mathematically stable coordinate transforms for wallpaper/kaleidoscope mappings.
Use signed-distance-field fragments for simple repeated patterns, vertex meshes for selected 3D objects.
Precompute bounded meshes outside render callback and cache by parameter signature.
Keep normal generation and winding consistent; cap subdivision and clip planes.
render_stages: Resolve preset, camera and symmetry parameters.
Generate/cache mesh when topology changes.
Render 2D SDF or 3D mesh scene using GL ES programs and depth state.
Apply simple post-process and export/present through VisualCore target.
design.engineering_rule: Use the shared VisualCore scene and camera APIs only if the audited API really supports these use cases; document missing requirements as upstream feature requests.

Mesh generation has index bounds and valid normals

Repeated preset transitions leave GPU objects stable

Track mesh cache hit/miss and upload stalls.
Provide lower-poly preview while expensive meshes are prepared.
risks: High tessellation spikes CPU/memory—mesh budget and async generation

design.summary: A modern audio-reactive visualizer with oscillograms, spectrum analysis and customizable graphics scenes that is not a ProjectM clone.
design.brainstorm_concept: A modern music visualization application with waveform displays, spectrum analysis, 3D environments, procedural visual effects, and customizable scenes.
design.primary_capability: authorized audio input, FFT and visual mapping
design.validity_risk: source capability honesty, callback safety, permissions
design.opportunity: A general-purpose visualization product that can share rendering technology with ProjectM without being a ProjectM clone.
audiences: People playing owned or in-app-controlled audio
journeys: Choose microphone or an app-owned audio file and grant permission where needed.

Calibrate gain, adjust colors and save a scene preset.
mvp_features: Microphone permission-gated live input and local file audio the app can legally decode
RMS, peak, FFT spectrum and smoothed beat-energy signals
Three visually different scenes: bars, waveform rings and 3D-ish responsive geometry
Source/status indicator and audio-interruption recovery
Parameter presets, local persistence and accessibility text metrics
Silent demo signal for offline testing
non_goals: Capturing protected/other apps system audio such as Spotify without supported APIs
Reusing MilkDrop engine code as default implementation
later_ideas: MIDI control and OSC-style controls if appropriate
Additional owned-file and streaming inputs via legal APIs
On-device visual recordings with clear consent

domain_types.name: ReactiveMapping
domain_types.contract: ReactiveMapping(feature, gain, attack, release, clamp, targetUniform)

algorithm_decisions: Use AVAudioEngine/AVAudioSession only for approved audio sources and handle route/interruptions explicitly.
Compute windowed FFT from bounded ring buffer outside realtime audio callback; avoid allocations/locks in callback.
Time-stamp audio features and interpolate/smooth parameters at render-frame boundary.
Keep source source/permission state separate from graphics and avoid assuming projectM audio capture API supports arbitrary apps.
render_stages: Acquire PCM from permitted source.
Convert to mono or per-channel visualization buffers and compute bounded features.
Smooth and map features to uniforms at frame cadence.
Render scene passes with VisualCore shaders; present or display silent demo fallback.
design.engineering_rule: Use only documented Apple audio sources; do not promise systemwide audio capture for streaming services. Clearly label demo signal versus real microphone/file inputs.
fixtures: Synthetic sine wave produces peak at expected FFT bin within tolerance
Silence yields zero/near-zero features and stable display
Audio callback never performs dynamic allocations on the hot path
Permission-denied path is still usable in demo mode
Interruption and route-change transitions do not leave audio engine or EGL state stuck
profiling: Monitor audio callback underruns, feature latency and render p95 frame time independently.
Maintain realtime-safe callback policy and bounded ring buffer.
Throttle heavy FFT/graphics work on thermal pressure without altering capture consent.
risks: iOS generally does not expose arbitrary other-app audio capture—market supported inputs only
Audio route/device timing varies—timestamp and smooth feature transfer
Sharing code with ProjectM could accidentally import ProjectM-specific logic—enforce module boundary

design.opportunity: A polished ambient experience with customizable aquariums, creatures, environments, and behaviors.

Bounded 2D/2.5D school behaviors and swim animation
Tap-to-feed and decoration placement gestures
Bubbles, caustics, depth layers and environmental particles

Low-motion/low-power ambient mode with auto dimming
non_goals: Realistic ecosystem or animal care simulator

algorithm_decisions: Use bounded steering forces for separation, alignment and cohesion with a small neighbor search.
Fish orientation and fin animation follow velocity with smoothed heading.
Keep habitat edits deterministic and separately serialized from transient fish motion.
Reuse sprites/materials by species, batch draw calls and soft-mask water effects.
render_stages: Load habitat assets and document state.
Update fish agents and plant animations in fixed steps.
Render depth-ordered background, fauna, vegetation, bubbles and caustics.

Allow user-defined quality and low-power sleep behavior.

risks: Asset provenance and third-party artwork licensing are central—ship only owned/licensed media

AI-generated motion can look erratic—use capped forces and animation smoothing

design.summary: A compact collection of highly legible arcade games with glow, particles and disciplined game logic.
design.brainstorm_concept: A collection of visually distinctive arcade games built around simple mechanics, glowing effects, particle systems, and procedural backgrounds.

design.opportunity: A collection of small, polished games with a consistent visual identity.

mvp_features: One complete game first: Neon Dodge with player lane, falling hazards and collectible orbs
Deterministic fixed-step update loop and authoritative collision rules
Start/pause/restart/game-over flows with local scores
Touch steering with configurable sensitivity
Particles, glow and visual feedback constrained by game readability
Sound/haptic toggles and reduced-flash controls
non_goals: An entire arcade collection before first release
Unmoderated online leaderboards or user-generated levels

domain_types.name: GameRun
domain_types.contract: GameRun(seed, elapsedTicks, score, lives, paused, waveIndex)

algorithm_decisions: Advance game world with fixed delta tick independent of display frame rate.
Use continuous or swept collision for fast moving hazards to prevent tunneling.
Separate collision geometry from sprites and post-effects.
Serialize deterministic input events for test replays; render may interpolate but never decides hit outcomes.
render_stages: Process touch input into intent vector.
Run input and wave spawning on fixed-step simulation.
Resolve collision/scoring on CPU domain model.
Render layered sprites, hazards, additive glow and feedback particles through VisualCore.
design.engineering_rule: Keep graphics effects a VisualCore client, not the authoritative game simulation. Visual readability is a functional acceptance criterion.
fixtures: Recorded input replay produces identical score and collision ticks
Background/resume freezes simulation rather than catching up
Swept collision catches high-speed hazards
High score is not corrupted by abrupt termination
Hitboxes remain readable when bloom quality settings change
profiling: Prioritize predictable input-to-action latency and p95 frame time.
Measure overdraw and avoid full-screen expensive bloom on low tiers.
Run 30 and 60 Hz timing tests for equivalent simulation outcomes.
risks: Effects that obscure obstacles hurt playability—cap bloom and preserve contrast
Frame-rate-dependent game logic causes inconsistent difficulty—fixed timestep
Additional games multiply maintenance—ship one vertical slice and validate retention

mvp_features: 2D circles and boxes with rigid-body collision

Object spawn, grab, pin and delete gestures

non_goals: Real 3D soft bodies or fluid solver

domain_types.name: PhysicsBody
domain_types.contract: PhysicsBody(id, shape, mass, inertia, pose, velocity, restitution, friction)

algorithm_decisions: Start with a fixed-step CPU 2D solver and broadphase for a small object count.
Use impulse-based collision with restitution/friction and conservative positional correction.
Apply spring forces with stability guardrails and bounded stiffness for chosen dt.
Compute diagnostics separately; explicitly label results as educational approximations.
render_stages: Collect editor operations.
Advance force accumulator, broadphase and narrowphase collision.
Solve constraints and integrate poses at bounded fixed time step.
Upload transforms and draw rigid bodies, vector arrows and contact effects.
design.engineering_rule: Do not offload simulation into a shader merely because VisualCore offers GPUs; choose CPU deterministic baseline and use VisualCore strictly for visualization.
fixtures: Two-body elastic collision approximates expected momentum within solver tolerance
Resting stack remains bounded over long runs
Mass zero is treated as static and never divided by zero
Spring energy test has known bounded behavior
Identical initial state and event stream reproduce deterministic CPU results
profiling: Measure CPU solver time separately from GPU draw time.
Maintain maximum active-body budget and optional sleep detection.
Reduced-quality mode lowers draw complexity without changing simulation laws.
risks: Numerical instability from large dt or stiff springs—fixed substeps and parameter caps
Users may assume engineering accuracy—document educational model and units
Object count may grow without limit—enforce scene budget

design.summary: A precise, tactile light-reflection puzzle game with visually rich beams and deterministic rules.
design.brainstorm_concept: A puzzle game involving beams of light, mirrors, reflections, portals, and dynamic geometric environments.
design.validity_risk: ray intersection/snap rules and level solver
design.opportunity: A visually distinctive puzzle game with increasingly complex mechanics.
journeys: Rotate a mirror to redirect a beam into target sensor.

later_ideas: Additional beam colors, splitters and portals
Level editor and local puzzle packs
algorithm_decisions: Compute ray/segment intersection on CPU from exact grid geometry; treat shader beam rendering as presentation only.
Avoid self-intersection with explicit epsilon and last-hit tracking; cap bounces and detect cycles.
Propagate color channels through splitters only when authored in rules; start with monochrome in Phase 1.
Use solver/replay tests to verify solutions and guard against unintended shortcuts.
render_stages: Apply user mirror edit to immutable grid snapshot.
Recompute beam tree and sensor states on CPU.
Generate glowing beam quads from exact segments, render mirrors, walls and targets.
Animate solved feedback without changing logical results.
design.engineering_rule: Formal puzzle rules and level validation matter more than animation features. A shader must never decide if the puzzle is solved.
fixtures: Incidence angle equals reflection angle within tolerance
Repeating mirror loops end at bounded bounce budget
All shipping levels have at least one verified solution
Undo restores exact previous grid and beam state
Beam visual endpoints match ray solver coordinates
profiling: Low scene complexity; optimize latency and deterministic state changes rather than throughput.
Keep bloom capped so color-coded logic stays legible.
Use battery-friendly idle rendering when puzzle state is unchanged.
risks: Visual beams can diverge from logical paths—single source of truth in CPU tracer
Puzzle content is expensive to design—ship small validated set
Touch rotation imprecision—snap to grid and provide large tap targets

Prefer static starfield and bounded orbit geometry to heavy postprocessing.
Test long timescales for numerical issues and UI date overflow.

algorithm_decisions: Parse XYZ with limits on atoms, lines and UTF-8 length; explicit unit and format validation.
If bond connectivity is inferred from distances, label it as an estimate and apply element-specific conservative thresholds.

render_stages: Load trusted bundled or validated XYZ molecule.

fixtures: XYZ parser rejects negative atom counts, NaNs and oversized files

Atom selection is correct for camera transforms and occlusion policy
Bond inference is deterministic and marked inferred
Model switch and orientation restore do not leak buffers
profiling: Cap atoms/bonds and draw calls by device tier; fail clearly before OOM.
Normalize geometry to avoid precision loss.
Use quality tiers for tessellation while keeping selection and labels legible.
risks: Untrusted molecule files may exhaust memory—strict parsers and size caps
Inferred bonds can be scientifically wrong—metadata labels and explicit-source preference

design.pitch: Weave and phase-shift 3D luminous ribbons into target harmonies
